snippet.title: The Mafat Conspiracy (NES) Playthrough
snippet.description:
A playthrough of Vic Tokai's 1990 license-based action-adventure game for the NES, The Mafat Conspiracy. 

Though the front of the box doesn't present it as such, The Mafat Conspiracy is the direct sequel to Vic Tokai's 1988 adult-oriented sleeper hit, Golgo 13: Top Secret Mission (https://youtu.be/qqVW5S21sAU).

The blurb on the back, however, holds nothing - and I mean nothing - back. This sales pitch is peak NES hype:

"CAUTION! OPENING THIS BOX UNLEASHES AN AWESOME ADVENTURE. A "Star Wars" satellite has been snatched out of orbit, the world edges toward nuclear oblivion, and the CIA and KGB are blaming each other. 

Golgo 13 is back just in time. The Mafat Conspiracy is a phantasmagoria of action and interaction. Your eyeballs will stretch from their sockets as you speed through Europe in Golgo's Ferrari. Your bones will rattle as you leap across the cars on the Orient Express. And if you think you've seen bad dudes, wait till you feel the power of Duke Togo's wicked karate kick. 

The Mafat Conspiracy is for those who demand the very best in video games. Open this box, and we'll prove it to you!"

Like Top Secret Episode, The Mafat Conspiracy is a multi-genre action cart driven by a thoroughly ludicrous Reagan-era, Cold War-inspired plot. Duke starts out by wandering the streets of Paris, shooting and kicking through droves of guys in suits and sunglasses, ducking into buildings for ammo and health pickups, and maneuvering his way through a few first-person mazes. He then jumps into his Ferrari for a Rad Racer-style vehicle combat sequence, and once he's arrived at his destination, he assembles his M-16 in order to snipe the pilot of a helicopter in hot pursuit. Providing he survives the ordeal, he heads back to the city streets to karate some more bad guys, and the game continues on like that for several acts before culminating in one of the slickest, most shamelessly violent endings to be seen on the NES.

The Mafat Conspiracy has a lot in common with its precursor, but the feel of the game is quite different, probably due to the change in developers. Top Secret Episode was developed by Cyclone System, and the sequel was handled by Aicom. 

The differences in the teams' styles and approaches can be seen in their other NES works. Cyclone's WURM (https://youtu.be/tFleuEYX-W0), which inherited much of Top Secret Mission's DNA, feels like a spiritual successor to that game. The Mafat Conspiracy, on the other hand, feels like a slightly gawky middle child in Aicom's line-up of cutscene-heavy NES platformers, landing squarely between Astyanax (https://youtu.be/ra0Avl41NlA) and Vice: Project Doom (https://youtu.be/4Bhu7SqkPl8).

That is to say, The Mafat Conspiracy is a polished, flashy, and fun game, but it feels more "commercial" than the first. Top Secret Episode was the edgy game equivalent of an R-rated thriller steeped in politics, the story had teeth and a message, and its gameplay was loaded with innovative touches that helped it to better serve the narrative. The Mafat Conspiracy is more a PG-13, popcorn-friendly summer blockbuster. The production values have been ramped up, the challenge has been dialed way down, and the substance was sacrificed to give it more mass appeal. The sheer number of cutscenes speaks to this: consider how, of the twenty minutes it takes to reach Act 2 (19:37) in this playthrough, only eight are given to proper gameplay. The plot is simpler and safer than Top Secret Mission's, and it's not an integral part of the experience this time around. Despite the time The Mafat Conspiracy dedicates to it, the story is ultimately disposable. The cutscenes could've been axed and you'd still have been left with a solid action game.

The Mafat Conspiracy is worth playing. The graphics and music are excellent, the controls are smooth, and the game entertains. My only complaint is that, by broadening its general appeal, Aicom missed the boat on what made Top Secret Episode so special. If you loved Top Secret Mission, this will probably feel a bit soulless. If you didn't like Top Secret Episode, you'll probably find The Mafat Conspiracy to be far more agreeable. 
_____________
No cheats were used during the recording of this video. 

NintendoComplete (http://www.nintendocomplete.com/) punches you in the face with in-depth reviews, screenshot archives, and music from classic 8-bit NES games!
